subject: music
topicDisplay: Area Of Study 3 Music For Film
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In music production, 'panning' controls...?
options: The tempo of the sequencer
The amount of reverb on a track
The placement of a sound within the stereo field (left to right)
The overall loudness of the master
questions.explain: Panning positions a sound across the stereo image from left to right.

questions.q: 'Scat singing' in jazz is...?
options: A whispered, breathy vocal effect
Singing only the written lyrics with no variation
Singing in strict unison with the bass line
Vocal improvisation using nonsense syllables to imitate an instrument
questions.explain: Scat singing improvises wordless, nonsense syllables, treating the voice like an improvising instrument.

questions.q: A 'riff' in rock and pop music is best defined as...?
options: A sudden change of key
A gradual increase in tempo
A solo improvised cadenza
A short, repeated melodic or rhythmic pattern, often instrumental
questions.explain: A riff is a short, catchy pattern repeated throughout a song, frequently as an instrumental hook.

questions.q: Swing-era big bands such as Count Basie's typically organised their players into which sectional layout?
options: Choir, organ and percussion
Solo piano with string quartet
Strings, woodwind and brass
Saxophones, brass (trumpets/trombones) and rhythm section
questions.explain: Big bands are built around a saxophone section, a brass section and a rhythm section.

questions.q: The standard twelve-bar blues progression in its basic form follows which sequence of chords (in bars)?
options: I-vi-IV-V repeated three times
I-I-IV-IV / V-V-I-I / IV-IV-V-V
I-IV-I-V / I-IV-I-V / I-IV-I-V
I-I-I-I / IV-IV-I-I / V-IV-I-I
questions.explain: The classic twelve-bar blues uses four bars of I, two of IV returning to I, then V-IV-I across the final four bars.

questions.q: Modal jazz, exemplified by Miles Davis's 'So What', is distinguished from bebop chiefly by its...?
options: Complete absence of improvisation
Reliance on rapid chord changes every two beats
Strict adherence to twelve-bar blues form
Use of static modes/scales held over long stretches rather than frequent chord changes
questions.explain: Modal jazz bases improvisation on slow-moving modes held for many bars, freeing soloists from rapid chord changes.

questions.q: The effect known as 'delay' produces which result?
options: A widening of the stereo field by phase inversion
One or more distinct repeats (echoes) of the original signal
A panning of sound between left and right speakers
A smoothing of dynamic range
questions.explain: Delay creates discrete repeats, or echoes, of the original sound.

questions.q: In film music, a 'leitmotif' is...?
options: A piece of source music heard within the scene
A recurring musical theme associated with a particular character, place or idea
A sudden silence used for dramatic effect
The opening title sequence music
questions.explain: A leitmotif is a recurring theme linked to a specific character, place or idea, a technique developed by Wagner and used widely in film.

questions.q: In film music, 'underscoring' (or underscore) most accurately means...?
options: Background music supporting a scene's mood or action, typically not heard by the characters
A loud climactic fanfare during the titles
The lyrics printed beneath a song
Music that the on-screen characters can hear (diegetic music)
questions.explain: Underscoring is non-diegetic background music that supports a scene's emotional or dramatic content.

questions.q: In a 'verse-chorus' pop structure, a 'pre-chorus' serves to...?
options: Build anticipation and lead smoothly from the verse into the chorus
Provide an instrumental solo break
Repeat the intro exactly
Replace the chorus entirely
questions.explain: The pre-chorus builds momentum and links the verse to the chorus.

questions.q: Free jazz, associated with Ornette Coleman's album 'Free Jazz' and later John Coltrane, is best described as...?
options: Big-band music with written-out arrangements only
Jazz that abandons fixed chord progressions, metre and predetermined structures in favour of collective spontaneity
A return to strict ragtime forms
A commercial dance style with simple harmonies
questions.explain: Free jazz dispenses with fixed harmony, metre and structure, prioritising collective, spontaneous improvisation.

questions.q: In jazz performance, 'swung' quavers are most accurately understood as pairs of quavers played roughly as...?
options: Two dotted-quaver semiquaver pairs
Two equal eighth notes
A triplet feel, long-short (approximately quarter-eighth of a triplet)
A short-long anticipation on every beat
questions.explain: Swung quavers approximate a triplet division, giving a long-short 'lilt' to each pair.

questions.q: Motown, the Detroit-based label of the 1960s, is associated with which of the following hallmarks?
options: Renaissance polyphony
Atonal twelve-tone writing
A polished soul-pop sound with the 'Funk Brothers' house band, tambourine back-beats and call-and-response vocals
Free improvisation with no fixed form
questions.explain: Motown produced a slick soul-pop sound built on a house band, back-beat percussion and gospel-derived call-and-response vocals.

questions.q: Early rock 'n' roll of the 1950s (e.g. Chuck Berry) frequently combined the twelve-bar blues with which other key ingredient?
options: Irregular metres such as 7/8
Through-composed orchestral textures
Gregorian chant melodies
A backbeat emphasising beats 2 and 4
questions.explain: Rock 'n' roll fused the twelve-bar blues with a strong backbeat on beats 2 and 4.

questions.q: The 'blue notes' that give the blues scale its characteristic flavour are most typically the flattened third, flattened fifth and flattened...?
options: Sixth
Fourth
Second
Seventh
questions.explain: The blues scale lowers the third, fifth and seventh degrees, producing the expressive 'blue' inflections.

questions.q: The studio effect 'reverb' is used to...?
options: Speed up the tempo of a track
Simulate the natural reflections of a sound in a space, adding sense of depth/ambience
Shift the pitch of a vocal up an octave
Remove low-frequency rumble
questions.explain: Reverb recreates the reflections of a physical space, adding depth and ambience to a sound.

questions.q: The 32-bar 'AABA' song form, common in jazz standards, consists of...?
options: A continuous through-composed structure
Four eight-bar sections where the third (B) provides a contrasting 'bridge'
A twelve-bar blues repeated until the soloist stops
Three identical sixteen-bar choruses
questions.explain: AABA form has four eight-bar sections, with the B section serving as a contrasting bridge.

questions.q: In music production, 'multitracking' refers to...?
options: Compressing a stereo mix into mono
Removing reverb from a recording
Playing many instruments live in one take with no overdubs
Recording different parts onto separate tracks so they can be balanced and edited independently
questions.explain: Multitracking records parts on separate tracks, allowing independent editing and mixing.

questions.q: Which jazz style, emerging in the 1940s, is defined by fast tempos, complex chord substitutions and virtuosic improvisation, associated with Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie?
options: Cool jazz
Ragtime
Swing
Bebop
questions.explain: Bebop is the fast, harmonically complex and virtuosic jazz style pioneered by Parker and Gillespie.

questions.q: A 'hook' in popular music is best described as...?
options: A device for tuning the guitar
The final cadence of the song
A modulation to the relative minor
A short, catchy musical idea designed to grab the listener and stick in the memory
questions.explain: A hook is a memorable, catchy idea engineered to capture and hold the listener's attention.

questions.q: A 'walking bass' line in jazz is most characterised by which feature?
options: A steady stream of crotchets outlining the chords, usually one note per beat
Rapid arpeggiated semiquaver flourishes
A sustained pedal note held under the harmony
Syncopated off-beat stabs played pizzicato
questions.explain: A walking bass moves in even crotchets, typically one note per beat, threading through the chord tones to drive the harmony forward.

questions.q: In song structure terminology, a 'bridge' (or 'middle eight') typically functions to...?
options: Provide contrast in melody/harmony before returning to the chorus or verse
State the main hook for the first time
End the song with a fade-out
Repeat the intro material exactly
questions.explain: The bridge offers contrasting material that breaks up verse-chorus repetition before a return.

questions.q: Ragtime, popularised by Scott Joplin, is principally characterised by which rhythmic device?
options: A swung shuffle feel in the bass
A syncopated, off-beat melody set against a steady march-like bass
Rubato throughout with no fixed pulse
Continuous polyrhythmic layering of three rhythms
questions.explain: Ragtime sets a syncopated right-hand melody against a regular, march-style stride bass.

questions.q: In a typical pop or rock song, the section designed to be the most memorable and which usually contains the title and main hook is the...?
options: Verse
Intro
Chorus
Bridge
questions.explain: The chorus is the most memorable section, typically stating the title and main hook.

questions.q: 'Sequencing' in music production primarily involves...?
options: Adding distortion to a guitar amplifier
Conducting a live orchestra
Arranging musical events (often MIDI) in time on a DAW timeline for playback or editing
Mastering a finished album for vinyl
questions.explain: Sequencing arranges and edits musical events, frequently MIDI data, along a timeline for playback.

questions.q: In the standard jazz turnaround, a ii-V-I progression in the key of C major uses which three chords in order?
options: Dm7 – G7 – Fmaj7
Dm7 – G7 – Cmaj7
Em7 – A7 – Dmaj7
Cmaj7 – F7 – G7
questions.explain: In C major the supertonic seventh is Dm7, the dominant seventh is G7 and the tonic is Cmaj7.

questions.q: The typical jazz 'rhythm section' that accompanies soloists usually comprises which combination?
options: Violin, viola and cello
Piano (or guitar), double bass and drums
Clarinet, flute and oboe
Trumpet, trombone and saxophone
questions.explain: The rhythm section conventionally consists of a chordal instrument (piano/guitar), bass and drums.

questions.q: In the genre of the stage musical, an 'I want' song typically functions to...?
options: Express a principal character's central desire or goal early in the show
Provide comic relief only
Resolve the plot in the finale
Underscore a scene change instrumentally
questions.explain: The 'I want' song establishes the protagonist's driving desire, usually near the start of a musical.

questions.q: The film-scoring technique 'mickey-mousing' refers to...?
options: Recording the score before filming begins
Improvised jazz played over the closing credits
Music that closely mirrors and synchronises with on-screen action, beat for beat
Using cartoon sound effects in live-action films
questions.explain: Mickey-mousing matches the music precisely to on-screen movement, a hallmark of early animation scoring.

questions.q: In jazz harmony, 'comping' refers to...?
options: Composing a fully notated arrangement in advance
Compressing the dynamic range in the mix
A pianist or guitarist playing improvised, syncopated chordal accompaniment behind a soloist
Counting the band in before a number
questions.explain: Comping is the improvised, rhythmic chordal accompaniment provided by piano or guitar behind a soloist.
